entities.name: Vinack's stepson
entities.description: A farmer and the narrator, who hated his stepfather Vinack, runs the farm after his mother's death, and lets Vinack walk to his death before the minotaurs.

entities.name: Vinack
entities.description: A feared monster-slaying hero, a living legend on the Arkos border, who abused the narrator's family, and who sacrifices himself to the minotaur oracle.

entities.name: Narrator's mother
entities.description: The narrator's mother, who married Vinack out of necessity but came to love him, and who died when the narrator was seventeen.

entities.name: Narrator's father
entities.description: The narrator's father, who died in an accident with a load of grain or rocks.

entities.name: Zerili
entities.description: A young scholar who argued for a treaty with the minotaurs and was found mutilated a week later.

entities.name: Minotaur oracle
entities.description: A large minotaur seer, rumored to have the ear of Mogis, who directs the raids and kills Vinack with a blow to the head and a blood ritual.

entities.name: Minotaurs
entities.description: Raiding minotaur tribes in the borderlands that demand human tribute.

entities.name: Mogis
entities.description: The god of slaughter, whose shape the narrator thinks he glimpses behind the oracle.

entities.name: Athreos
entities.description: The god who judges the dead when they cross the river.

entities.name: Heliod
entities.description: A god whose ways the narrator says he does not understand.

entities.name: Pharika
entities.description: A god whose disciples the narrator sought remedies from.

entities.name: Akroan soldier
entities.description: A soldier on deployment who joked about Zerili's death.

entities.name: Arkos
entities.description: A polis next to the border region where the narrator lives.

entities.name: Kendraki Provinces
entities.description: The human villages north of the minotaur lands that Vinack's sacrifice protects.

entities.name: Theros
entities.description: The plane of gods and heroes.

events.summary: The narrator's mother marries Vinack when the narrator is ten, after the narrator was beaten by farmhands' sons.
events.quote: When I was ten when my mother married him and, at the time, I didn't hate him.

events.summary: The narrator confronts Vinack after seeing his mother's bruised face, and Vinack strikes him.
events.quote: He told me to know my place and struck me in the head.

events.summary: The narrator tells Vinack he is a selfish beast, and Vinack beats him until the mother and farmhands throw him out.
The narrator's mother dies of failing health when he is seventeen, leaving him in charge of the farmland.
events.quote: My mother passed away when I was seventeen and I was then in charge of our farmland.

events.summary: The scholar Zerili argues for a treaty with the minotaurs and is found murdered and mutilated that week.
events.quote: the young man's mutilated corpse was found later that week

events.summary: Vinack returns after ten years asking for help against the minotaurs, and the narrator strikes him.
events.quote: I would not have struck him if he hadn't said, "I need your help, Son."

events.summary: The narrator agrees to help and Vinack proposes striking down the minotaur oracle.
events.quote: Vinack's plan was to go into their territory and strike down their oracle.

events.summary: The narrator searches Zerili's home and ledger and concludes that the village secretly pays human tribute and that Vinack means him to die.
events.quote: Vinack meant for me to die.

events.summary: At the minotaur camp the narrator presses a dagger to Vinack's back, and Vinack reveals the sacrifice will be himself.
events.quote: "No, Son," he said, shaking his head. "The sacrifice will be me."

events.summary: Vinack offers himself as sacrifice to the oracle, who crushes and snaps his body, and a blood mist fills the minotaurs while the narrator thinks he sees Mogis.
events.quote: Without ceremony, the shaman slammed his fist downwards on Vinack's head, pushing it down into his body.

events.summary: The narrator returns to the village praised as the hero who stopped the minotaur menace, and concludes he hates himself.
events.quote: I let that man walk to his death.

relations.note: He married her, becoming the narrator's stepfather.
relations.quote: I hate the man who married my mother.
